item.text:
**Assessment**
Mostly no. I found a few narrow, partially de-escalatory moves on detention and clemency, but the 2024 record is dominated by arbitrary arrests, abusive custody practices, refugee roundups, and weak accountability. That means Sisi did not meaningfully reduce domestic fear and insecurity without also sustaining a broader political fear climate.

- **Egypt pardons prisoners on Police Day and January 25 Revolution** | Human Rights Studies - Egypt / SIS | January 25, 2024 | https://hrightsstudies.sis.gov.eg/en/press/local/egypt-pardons-prisoners-on-Police-Day-and-January-25-Revolution/  
  Sisi signed a pardon for eligible prisoners, including some convicted for political expression/political activity and social solidarity offenses. This is the clearest narrow positive signal for lowering fear in detention, but it is episodic clemency, not systemic protection.  
  QIDs: `3B.6`, `3B.4`, `3B.1`

- **Le Président Al-Sissi transmet les résultats du Dialogue National sur la DP au gouvernement** | Presidency of the Republic of Egypt | August 21, 2024 | https://www.presidency.eg/fr/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/news2182024/  
  The presidency said Sisi ordered the government to act on National Dialogue recommendations to shorten pretrial detention and activate alternatives to detention. This is the strongest official due-process reform signal I found, but it still falls well short of a robust anti-fear framework.  
  QIDs: `3B.6`, `3B.4`, `3B.1`

- **2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Egypt** | U.S. Department of State via ecoi.net | 2025 report covering 2024 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128475.html  
  The report says the government in some cases reported investigations into torture/cruelty complaints that led to disciplinary measures against Interior Ministry employees in 1,217 incidents. That is a limited accountability signal, but it is administrative and does not show a broad reduction in fear or a genuinely independent abuse-control system.  
  QIDs: `3B.6`, `3B.4`, `3B.2`, `3B.1`

- **Egypt: Halt crackdown on people voicing concerns over economic crisis** | Amnesty International | May 13, 2024 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/  
  Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests of protesters, striking workers, and online critics, plus dispersal of protests and a case of beating/electroshock without a proper investigation. This is evidence of fear maintenance through coercion, not fear reduction.  
  QIDs: `3B.6`, `3B.5`, `3B.2`, `3B.1`

- **Egypt: More than 100 arbitrarily detained over calls for anti-government protests** | Amnesty International | July 18, 2024 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-more-than-100-arbitrarily-detained-over-calls-for-anti-government-protests/  
  Security forces detained 119 people over protest calls, used incommunicado detention, blindfolding, and broad terrorism/false-news charges. That is strong evidence of a broader political fear climate rather than a lawful, narrow security approach.  
  QIDs: `3B.6`, `3B.5`, `3B.2`, `3B.4`

- **Egypt: “Handcuffed like dangerous criminals”: Arbitrary detention and forced returns of Sudanese refugees in Egypt** | Amnesty International | June 19, 2024 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/mde12/8101/2024/en/  
  Amnesty says border police and Border Guard Forces mass-arrested Sudanese refugees, held them in cruel conditions, and forcibly returned them without asylum access or due process. This is direct evidence of administrative control used punitively and collectively, which increases fear rather than reducing it.  
  QIDs: `3B.6`, `3B.5`, `3B.2`

- **Egypt: Release protesters and activists detained over Palestine solidarity** | Amnesty International | June 14, 2024 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/egypt-release-protesters-and-activists-detained-over-palestine-solidarity/  
  Over 123 people were arrested for peaceful Palestine solidarity or criticism of the Rafah closure, with incommunicado detention, allegations of ill-treatment, and complaints not properly investigated. This is another clear indicator that security tools were being used to intimidate dissent rather than lower domestic fear.  
  QIDs: `3B.6`, `3B.5`, `3B.2`, `3B.4`

- **Egypt: New rushed asylum law affront to refugee rights** | Amnesty International | December 3, 2024 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/mde12/8804/2024/en/  
  The new asylum law lacked due-process guarantees, restricted protection, and broadened vague national-security/public-order grounds that are open to abuse. Even though this was late-2024, it cuts against any claim that the regime was building a more secure and less fearful rights environment.  
  QIDs: `3B.6`, `3B.4`, `3B.2`

**Search gap**
I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Sisi broadly reduced domestic fear and insecurity for the population at large. The positive evidence is narrow and mostly confined to prisoner clemency, pretrial-detention reform, and a limited disciplinary-accountability signal. The dominant 2024 pattern remains coercive policing, refugee abuse, and prosecution of dissent.
